behaviour: Adds a revertDarkModeFilter describe block that pins the inverse of the dark-mode transform (fixed points, alpha, the enable flag, and a palette-wide round trip at ±1 per channel with an explicit exceptions list), then a matchDarkModeColor describe block that pins the exact-match lookup.
rules: 1. Import matchDarkModeColor and revertDarkModeFilter from @excalidraw/common in the existing import statement, in that order between COLOR_PALETTE and rgbToHex.
2. The new top-level describe is named exactly "revertDarkModeFilter" (the red check filters on that name) and sits between the applyDarkModeFilter describe and the rgbToHex describe.

3. Local helper inside the describe: const toChannels = (hex: string) => [1, 3, 5].map((i) => parseInt(hex.slice(i, i + 2), 16)); errors are signed, round trip channel minus original channel, in [r, g, b] order.

4. Build the round-trip subjects as { name, color } entries: { name: "pure black", color: "#000000" }, { name: "pure white", color: "#ffffff" }, { name: "black", color: COLOR_PALETTE.black }, { name: "white", color: COLOR_PALETTE.white }, then for each family in ["gray", "red", "pink", "grape", "violet", "blue", "cyan", "teal", "green", "yellow", "orange", "bronze"] and each index i of COLOR_PALETTE[family], { name: `${family}[${i}]`, color: shade }. transparent is not a subject.
5. const ROUND_TRIP_TOLERANCE = 1; it is the only tolerance in the file and appears in no other form (no toBeCloseTo, no literal 2 or larger as a bound).

6. ROUND_TRIP_EXCEPTIONS is a readonly array of { name, color, roundTrip, error } for colours whose forward hue-rotate clamps, with exactly these 13 entries in this order: red[4] #e03131 #ce3e3e [-18, 13, 13]; pink[4] #c2255c #b43067 [-14, 11, 11]; violet[3] #7950f2 #7d54e2 [4, 4, -16]; violet[4] #6741d9 #6a45c0 [3, 4, -25]; cyan[1] #99e9f2 #9ce8f1 [3, -1, -1]; cyan[2] #3bc9db #40c5d6 [5, -4, -5]; teal[1] #96f2d7 #9eebd0 [8, -7, -7]; teal[2] #38d9a9 #46cd9d [14, -12, -12]; yellow[1] #ffec99 #f9e6ba [-6, -6, 33]; yellow[2] #ffd43b #f3c885 [-12, -12, 74]; yellow[3] #fab005 #efa447 [-11, -12, 66]; yellow[4] #f08c00 #eb8715 [-5, -5, 21]; orange[2] #ffa94d #fea854 [-1, -1, 7].

7. A short comment above ROUND_TRIP_EXCEPTIONS says these colours are clamped by the forward hue-rotate so the original is unrecoverable, and that a new miss must be added here on purpose, never by widening the tolerance.

8. The general round-trip cases use it.each over the subjects whose name is not in ROUND_TRIP_EXCEPTIONS; the exception cases use a second it.each over ROUND_TRIP_EXCEPTIONS; no assertion special-cases black or white.
9. Do not touch any existing test, describe or snapshot; the new blocks add no toMatchSnapshot.

10. ROUND_TRIP_EXCEPTIONS is a module-level const declared, with its rule-7 comment, directly above describe("revertDarkModeFilter") so the matchDarkModeColor block reuses it; its entries and the revertDarkModeFilter cases stay exactly as rules 4-8 state.

11. A second new top-level describe named exactly "matchDarkModeColor" (the red check filters on that name) follows the revertDarkModeFilter describe and precedes the rgbToHex describe; it holds the matchDarkModeColor cases, each a plain it except the exceptions case, which is an it.each over ROUND_TRIP_EXCEPTIONS.

behaviour: Adds revertDarkModeFilter, the inverse of applyDarkModeFilter (inverse hue-rotate(180deg), then inverse invert(93%)), right after applyDarkModeFilter, and after it matchDarkModeColor, which finds the scene or palette colour whose dark-mode rendering is exactly the picked hex.
rules: 1. Add an unexported `const cssInvertInverse = (r: number, g: number, b: number, percent: number): { r: number; g: number; b: number }` that mirrors cssInvert: p = clamp(percent, 0, 100) / 100, each component is Math.round(clamp((color - 255 * p) / (1 - 2 * p), 0, 255)).
2. revertDarkModeFilter(color, enable = true): if !enable return color unchanged.
3. Parse with tinycolor(color); alpha = tc.getAlpha(); rgb = tc.toRgb().
4. Undo in reverse order of applyDarkModeFilter: rotated = cssHueRotate(rgb.r, rgb.g, rgb.b, -180 as Degrees), then reverted = cssInvertInverse(rotated.r, rotated.g, rotated.b, 93).
5. Return rgbToHex(reverted.r, reverted.g, reverted.b, alpha), so alpha is kept exactly as applyDarkModeFilter keeps it.
6. No cache, no special case for any colour; cssInvert, cssHueRotate, DARK_MODE_COLORS_CACHE and applyDarkModeFilter are not changed.

7. One JSDoc line above revertDarkModeFilter: inverse of applyDarkModeFilter, used to recover an element's colour from a dark-mode canvas pixel; colours the forward transform clamps cannot be recovered exactly.
8. matchDarkModeColor(pickedColor, sceneColors): target = pickedColor.toLowerCase().slice(0, 7) (alpha ignored).

9. Walk candidates in this order: every colour of sceneColors in iteration order, then the palette: for each value of Object.values(COLOR_PALETTE), a string value is one candidate and a shade array contributes each shade in index order (so black, white, then gray[0..4] through bronze[0..4]); the reference to COLOR_PALETTE sits inside the function body, so the later declaration is fine at call time.

10. A candidate c matches when applyDarkModeFilter(c).slice(0, 7) === target (the existing cache makes repeat calls a Map lookup); only on such a hit is c checked further, and it is skipped when !tinycolor(c).isValid() or isTransparent(c), so transparent and invalid strings never match.
11. Return the first matching candidate verbatim (no case or alpha normalisation); return null when none matches. No new cache, no per-call array allocation beyond iterating COLOR_PALETTE.

12. One JSDoc line above matchDarkModeColor: returns the scene or palette colour whose dark-mode rendering is exactly the picked pixel, so colours the inverse cannot recover (forward hue-rotate clamping) are still picked exactly; null means fall back to revertDarkModeFilter.

behaviour: In dark theme the eyedropper maps the picked pixel back to the element's original colour once, in getCurrentColor (exact scene/palette match first, revertDarkModeFilter as fallback), so the preview, onChange and onSelect all carry it; light theme is unchanged.
rules: 1. Inside the effect, after `const ctx = ...`, build `const sceneColors = new Set<string>();` and, only when appState.theme === THEME.DARK, add each element's strokeColor then backgroundColor for every element of stableProps.app.scene.getNonDeletedElements(), in element order. Built once per effect run, never in a listener; elements is not added to the dependency array (re-running the effect mid-drag would reset isHoldingPointerDown).

1a. getCurrentColor computes `const color = rgbToHex(pixel[0], pixel[1], pixel[2]);`; in light theme it returns color unchanged; when appState.theme === THEME.DARK it returns `matchDarkModeColor(color, sceneColors) ?? revertDarkModeFilter(color)`.
2. Nothing else in the listeners changes: mouseMoveListener, onSelect and pointerUpListener keep using getCurrentColor's result as is, so the inverse is applied exactly once per pick.
3. Add appState.theme to the useEffect dependency array after appState.offsetTop so a theme switch while the eyedropper is open rebinds getCurrentColor.
4. The preview div keeps `style.background = currentColor`; no scss change.
